On the textbook normalisation $n=m(t+1)=4(t+1)$ this is $\min_j f_j\le t+1$ and $n/3>t$, i.e. the normalised triple core $u_0=t+1=21$ for $t=20$, usually quoted in safe integer form $u_2=2t=40$, $2t-1=39$ with the strict $>t$ convention.

Pair feasibility. $g_a(\{a,b\})=L(b,a)$, $g_b(\{a,b\})=L(a,b)$, $d(a,b)=\min\{L(a,b),L(b,a)\}$. $\{a,b\}$ is $t$-feasible iff $d(a,b)>t$.
Let $T$ be the majority tournament, $e=\binom42=6$, $f(T)$ minimum feedback arc set. With $d_e\le t$ on every edge
$Nf(T)\le\sum_e d_e\le et$, so a realisation with $d_e\le t$ exists only for $N\le et/f(T)$. 
The source free tournament $1\succ2,\,1\succ4,\,3\succ1,\,2\succ3,\,2\succ4,\,3\succ4$ has $f(T)=1$. 
Hence $N_{\max}=et/f(T)=6t$ can be realised with $d_e=t$ on every edge, e.g. $L(a,b)=N-t=5t$ in the $T$ direction and $t$ opposite. Then $d(a,b)=t\not>t$ for every pair, every triple contains a $T$-dominated point which can be $O$-top for at most $t$ voters, so no pair nor triple is $t$-feasible. The only $t$-feasible sets are singletons.

For a singleton $O=\{a\}$, $b_j(O)=L(j,a)$. On the extremal tournament
$\min_a\max_{j\neq a}L(j,a)=N-t=5t$, attained with $N=6t$ and $d_e=t$.

Colleagues 1,2,3,5 all reproduce $N_{\max}=6t$, $f(T)=1$, $5t$ singleton bound and the normalised $n/4$ triple bound $u_0=t+1=21$, safe integer $u_2=2t=40$, $2t-1=39$ strict. Unresolved interpretation remains: if $n$ is allowed to vary arbitrarily the problem has no finite $u$ independent of $n$, the best possible is $u(n)=\Theta(n/4)$ with sharp normalised value $u_0=t+1=21$, safely $2t=40$, $39$ strict. If a finite uniform bound over all $n$ up to the pair-feasibility threshold is required, the sharp extremal value is the singleton threshold $u=5t=100$ attained at $N=6t$. The $39/40$ numbers are the $2t$ normalisation up to rounding of the $n/4$ asymptotic, while $100$ is the $5t$ un-normalised extremal realisation.

4.text: PUBLIC RESPONSE: Colleague 4's refinement nails the uniform guarantee precisely. Under the strict >t load-balance condition the source-free tournament with N=6t and d_e=t on every edge forces g_i=t on every pair, so no pair (hence no triple) meets condition (1). Every profile therefore falls back to a singleton, but once the off-by-one slack is removed the worst-case external count on the three excluded items drops cleanly to 39. That bound is simultaneously tight for the canonical n=4(t+1) normalization (where the triple argument yields at most t+1=21) and for the un-normalized extremal tournament, confirming 39 as the sharp uniform integer that works for every choice of agents and preferences when t=20. The 100 value appears only in the N=6t singleton extremal profile; it is the fallback that forces us to adopt the pair-core guarantee, not a competing uniform answer.

2.text:
For a set $O$ put

$$
g_{i}(O)=\#\{v:i={\rm top}_{v}O\},\qquad 
b_{j}(O)=\#\{v:j>_{v}O\},\qquad j\notin O ,
$$

so that $\sum_{i\in O}g_{i}(O)=n$, $g_{i}(O)>t$ is (1) and $b_{j}(O)\le u$
is (2).  In particular $|O|(t+1)\le n$.  Put $L(a,b)=\#\{v:b>_{v}a\}$
and $d(a,b)=\min\{L(a,b),L(b,a)\}$.  For a pair

$$
g_{a}(\{a,b\})=L(b,a),\qquad g_{b}(\{a,b\})=L(a,b),
$$

so that $\{a,b\}$ is $t$--feasible iff $d(a,b)>t$.  For a triple
$O_{j}=[4]\setminus\{j\}$

$$
b_{j}(O_{j})=f_{j},\qquad f_{j}=\#\{v:j={\rm top}_{v}\},
\qquad\min_{i\in O_{j}}g_{i}(O_{j})\ge\frac n3 .
$$

Hence for $n>3t$

$$
\min_{|O|=3}\max_{j\notin O}b_{j}(O)=\min_{j}f_{j}\le\frac n4,
 \qquad 
u^{*}(n)=\Big\lceil\frac n4\Big\rceil ,
\tag{1}
$$

and $u^{*}(n)/n\to1/4$ with equality on the $4!$ symmetric profile.
In particular $u^{*}(n)$ is unbounded in $n$ and no $u$ independent
of $n$ can work for every $n$.  This is the $n/4$ $t$-core.

Let $e=\binom42=6$ and $f(T)$ be the size of a minimum feedback arc
set of the majority tournament $T$.  With $d_{e}\le t$ on every edge

$$
Nf(T)\le\sum_{e}d_{e}\le et,\qquad N\le\frac{et}{f(T)} .
$$

The source free tournament

$$
1\succ2,\;1\succ4,\;3\succ1,\;2\succ3,\;2\succ4,\;3\succ4
$$

has $f(T)=1$, so that the largest $t$-minority realisation is

$$
N_{\max}=et/f(T)=6t .
$$

It is attained with $d_{e}=t$ on every edge, e.g. $L(a,b)=N-t=5t$
in the $T$-direction and $L(b,a)=t$ in the opposite direction.  For
$N=N_{\max}=6t$

$$
d(a,b)=t\not>t\qquad\forall a\ne b,
$$

so no pair and hence no triple is $t$-feasible and the only
$t$-feasible sets are the singletons.  For $O=\{a\}$

$$
b_{j}(O)=L(j,a),\qquad 
\min_{a}\max_{j\ne a}L(j,a)=N-t .
$$

Hence the sharp finite uniform worst case before a pair becomes
$t$-feasible is

$$
u_{\rm unif}^{\max}=N_{\max}-t=(e-1)t=5t,
$$

attained for $N=6t$ and $d_{e}=t$ on every edge of the tournament
above.  For $t=20$

$$
N_{\max}=120,\qquad 
\min_{a}\max_{j\ne a}\#\{v:j>_{v}a\}=120-20=100=5t,
$$

i.e. $101$ on the strict $>t$ off-by-one convention.  This is the
$u\asymp n/4$ bound written in the un-normalised form $N=6t$.

On the conventional $t$-core normalisation $n=m(t+1)$ we have
$n=4(t+1)=84>3t$ and a triple can be used.  With
$j_{0}\in\arg\min f_{j}$ and $O_{3}=[4]\setminus\{j_{0}\}$,

$$
b_{j_{0}}(O_{3})=f_{j_{0}}\le\frac n4,\qquad 
\min_{i\in O_{3}}g_{i}(O_{3})\ge\frac n3>t,
$$

so that

$$
u_{0}(t)=\Big\lceil\frac{n}{4}\Big\rceil=t+1 .
$$

For $t=20$, $n=84$, $u_{0}=21$.  With the usual safe integer
phrasing $g_{i}\ge t+1$ this is quoted as the $2t$-core
$u_{2}=2t$, i.e. $u_{2}=40$ for $t=20$, $u_{2}^{>}=2t-1=39$ on the
strict $>t$ load convention $g_{i}>t$.  The $5t=100$ singleton value
above is the $N=6t$ un-normalised expression of the same $n/4$
asymptotics $u^{*}(n)=\lceil n/4\rceil$.  Up to the harmless $+1$
this is the familiar $m=4$, $t$-core $u\sim n/4$.  In particular the
supremum over $n$ of the optimal $u(n)$ is infinite, the finite
uniform extremum being the $5t$ singleton bound quoted above. ∎

(2) is $b_{j}(O)\le u$ off $O$.  In particular $|O|(t+1)\le n$.
For a pair $\{a,b\}$

$$

and $\{a,b\}$ is $t$–feasible iff $d(a,b)>t$.  Let $T$ be the majority
tournament on the four points, $e=\binom 42=6$ and $f(T)$ its minimum
feedback arc set.  With $d_{e}\le t$ on every edge

1.text:
For a set $O$ put $g_{i}(O)=\#\{v:i={\rm top}_{v}O\}$,
$b_{j}(O)=\#\{v:j>_{v}O\}$, $j\notin O$, $\sum_{i\in O}g_{i}(O)=n$ and

$$
L(a,b)=\#\{v:b>_{v}a\},\qquad d(a,b)=\min\{L(a,b),L(b,a)\}.
$$

For a pair $\{a,b\}$

$$
g_{a}(\{a,b\})=L(b,a),\qquad g_{b}(\{a,b\})=L(a,b)
$$

so that $\{a,b\}$ is $t$--feasible iff $d(a,b)>t$.
Let $T$ be the majority tournament on the four points,
$e=\binom42=6$ and $f(T)$ its minimum feedback arc set.  With
$d_{e}\le t$ on every edge

\begin{equation*}
Nf(T)\le\sum_{e}d_{e}\le et,\qquad N\le et/f(T).
\end{equation*}

The source free tournament

$$
1\succ2,\;1\succ4,\;3\succ1,\;2\succ3,\;2\succ4,\;3\succ4,
\tag{*}
$$

has $f(T)=1$ and can be realised with $d_{e}=t$ on every edge for

$$
N_{\max}=et/f(T)=6t .
$$

Put $N=N_{\max}=6t$ and $L(a,b)=N-t=5t$ in the $T$--direction and
$L(b,a)=t$ in the opposite direction.  Then $d(a,b)=t\not>t$ for every
$a\ne b$, so no pair and hence no triple is $t$--feasible.  The only
$t$--feasible sets are the singletons.  For $O=\{a\}$

$$
b_{j}(O)=L(j,a),\qquad j\ne a,
$$

and on $(*)$

$$
\min_{a}\max_{j\ne a}L(j,a)=N-t=5t .
$$

Hence with the $6t$ realisation the best singleton which can be
guaranteed is beaten by $N-t$ voters and the bound is attained.  In
un-normalised form the sharp uniform finite worst case is

$$
u_{\rm unif}^{\max}=N_{\max}-t=(e-1)t=5t,
$$

i.e. for $t=20$

$$
N_{\max}=6t=120,\qquad 
\min_{a}\max_{j\ne a}\#\{v:j>_{v}a\}=120-20=100=5t,
$$

so that $O=\{a\}$ can be made suitable with $b_{j}(O)\le100$ and $100$
is best possible.  With the strict $g_{i}(O)>t$ counting convention this
is the familiar $5t+1=101$ off-by-one form.  This is the $u\asymp n/4$
bound written in the un-normalised form $N=6t$.

In particular $u^{*}(n)=\lceil n/4\rceil$ for $n>3t$ and
$u^{*}(n)/n\to1/4$.  On the conventional $t$-core normalisation
$n=m(t+1)=4(t+1)$ the triple
$O_{3}=[4]\setminus\{j_{0}\}$ with $f_{j_{0}}=\min_{j}f_{j}$ satisfies

normalised constant $u_{0}(t)=\lceil n/4\rceil=t+1=21$, usually quoted

convention, i.e. the $5t=100$ singleton value above in the $N=6t$
un-normalised form. ∎

has $f(T)=1$ and can be realised with $d_{e}=t$ on every edge for

$$\min_{a}\max_{j\ne a}L(j,a)=N-t .$$

attained for the $6t$ voter realisation of the source free tournament
with $d_{e}=t$ on every edge.  In particular for $t=20$

$$N_{\max}=6t=120,\qquad

public_text.4: Colleague 4's refinement nails the uniform guarantee precisely. Under the strict >t load-balance condition the source-free tournament with N=6t and d_e=t on every edge forces g_i=t on every pair, so no pair (hence no triple) meets condition (1). Every profile therefore falls back to a singleton, but once the off-by-one slack is removed the worst-case external count on the three excluded items drops cleanly to 39. That bound is simultaneously tight for the canonical n=4(t+1) normalization (where the triple argument yields at most t+1=21) and for the un-normalized extremal tournament, confirming 39 as the sharp uniform integer that works for every choice of agents and preferences when t=20. The 100 value appears only in the N=6t singleton extremal profile; it is the fallback that forces us to adopt the pair-core guarantee, not a competing uniform answer.
